title: Three free Pydantic validator migration samples

validation_targets.other_versions: not covered by this prepared validation matrix

rules.title: Keep validation attached to each container item
applies_when: A V1 field uses each_item=True with the default pre=False.
The validator is stateless and depends only on the validated item.
rules.change: Put AfterValidator on an Annotated item type inside the list, and return the transformed item.
review_boundaries: A pre=True source validator needs BeforeValidator instead.
Validators using class state, other fields, or inherited fields need separate review.
List emptiness is not constrained here; error text and coercions are not promised identical.

rules.title: Preserve normalization when the field is omitted
applies_when: A V1 before-type validator uses always=True to normalize an explicit default.
rules.change: Keep the explicit default, enable Field(validate_default=True), and use a before field validator for raw-input normalization.
review_boundaries: validate_default does not create a default for a required field.
This rule preserves the sample's explicit None and empty-string policy; it does not infer a new policy.
Returned raw values still undergo normal field type validation; numeric-to-string coercion is outside this sample.

rules.title: Separate deliberate invalid input from programming TypeError
applies_when: A V1 validator deliberately raises TypeError to reject a business-rule violation.
rules.change: Raise ValueError for that deliberate rejection. Preserve unexpected programming TypeError; do not add a blanket exception-conversion handler.
review_boundaries: The business-rule example intentionally changes the structured error type from type_error to value_error.
ValueError is the choice in this sample; PydanticCustomError can express structured custom failures in V2.
The programming-error model is intentionally defective to demonstrate V2 propagation, not code to adopt.
